direction.statement: For any fixed-rent share sigma the closure multiplier 1 + theta_V/sigma_V is at least 1/(1 - theta_V) (sigma_V <= 1 - theta_V), against (b)'s ~1.00: cheaper labour makes machines cheaper, so the wage must fall further to hold the task margin. Across the whole admissible sigma range, root for root, participation is below (b)'s at years 6 and 15. sigma sets the size, not the sign.
direction.exceptions_note: like for like in the site — against (b) calibrated at the measured site (4.2% of GDP), at g0 0.01 and 0.02, root for root — the measured-site variant (ii)'s participation is below (b)'s at every date after the start; what remains: c_site_hi's real wage rises before falling (x1.092 at year 7.75), less than (b) at the measured site does at the same root (x1.819 at g0 0.01, x1.558 at g0 0.02); c_site_lo's labour share (Figure 7 basis) halves no earlier than (b)'s at the measured site: 8.75 vs 8.5 (b_site_g001_lo), 8.75 vs 8.75 (b_site_lo). Against (b) at its calibrated site (13% of the basket; not like for like in the site, kept as a readout): c_site_hi not below b_hi from year 9 (0.532 vs 0.490 at year 15)

rate_link.statement: Headroom and the multiplier are the same 1/sigma object: at a fixed task margin d ln(w/r)/d ln(rho + delta) = 1/sigma_V and d ln(w/r)/d ln gamma = 1 + theta_V/sigma_V. An economy that survives a sustained +5 pp rise in the required return (headroom >= 5 pp at the all-assets delta) has sigma_V at or above the bound below, which puts it at the mild end of the sweep.
rate_link.caveat: headroom in pp scales with delta (headroom / delta is invariant): at the equipment + IPP delta the same economy has 24.62 pp, so the bound depends on which delta the +5 pp is read against

open_items: WP2026-01's labour definition is unverified: its 'human effort' is split into college and non-college labour, which suggests the BEA-BLS integrated accounts, and those impute self-employed labour. theta_V (I-O compensation of employees) leaves proprietors' labour in NOS, which matters in construction, part of the bundle. If the labour target includes imputed self-employed labour, theta_V is understated against it, which would push toward a more severe result. The WP2026-01 PDF is not in the repository (pinning/effort README 'Known gaps').

Under the open reading the investment chain's imported content (0.1846 of build cost, 56% of sigma_V 0.3300) is modelled as the chain's fixed-quantity land b — paid as domestic rent, so it counts in model income (3.3% of it at the start; hence M8's GDP net of imports), and drawn from the endowment T that housing shares — not as an elastic import at a world price. As investment falls the chain's land is freed for housing: its share of T 0.311 -> 0.219 -> 0.077 -> 0.040 (years 0/6/10/15, central low root; (b) 0.637 -> 0.147). The sigma sweep brackets sigma's size, not this land-market channel; its direction on the paths is not quantified (readouts.import_as_land).

Under the open reading the consumption chain's own foreign content (0.094 of PCE) is left in the model's capital services (cs = 1 - labour - site), so the model makes it with machines; only the investment chain's imported content is a fixed-quantity cost. The model has no fixed-price import in the consumption basket. A probe that moves it into a site-like fixed rent (site target 0.224, sigma held) points toward a more severe result: it has no root at g0 0.01 (its largest g0 is 0.00756), and at g0 0.005 participation at year 15 is 0.196 / 0.286 (low / high root) against the central's 0.223 / 0.387 at the same g0 — so the open reading's choice here is the mild one (readouts.pce_import_probe).
delta_chain (the normal return in sigma's construction) is BEA's private equipment + IPP rate, not the depreciation rate of the chain's own capital (FA 3.1ESI / 3.4ESI by industry would give it).

The tot-consistent labour prices PCE's foreign content at the domestic PCE chain's labour share (0.47/(1 - 0.094)); pricing it at theta_V instead gives 0.5232 and a lower g0 bound. The WP2026-01 numbers are a digitisation of its Figure 9.
